name: Cold Coffee

ingredients.name: Instant coffee powder (e.g. Nescafe Classic, Bru)

equipment: Blender (or a hand blender with a tall jug): blends the drink to a froth in 20-30 seconds
Tall glass (300 ml or more): so the froth has room
Small cup or bowl and a spoon: to dissolve the coffee and sugar
Measuring spoons and a measuring jug (or use the household measures)
Kettle or a small pan: only for 1 tbsp of warm water

steps.title: Chill the milk
steps.text: Keep 200 ml milk in the fridge for at least 1 hour beforehand.
steps.visualCue: The milk carton or jug feels cold to the touch and has fridge condensation on the outside
steps.cameraCheck: The cold milk jug or carton, with the 200 ml mark or measuring jug in view
steps.videoShot: Milk poured from the fridge into a measuring jug up to 200 ml.
steps.watchOut: Using room-temperature milk, which makes a thin drink that melts the ice quickly; if you forgot, put the milk in the freezer for 15 min and use 1 extra ice cube.

steps.title: Measure the coffee and sugar
steps.text: Put 1.5 tsp instant coffee and 3 tsp sugar into a small cup.
steps.visualCue: Two level small heaps in the cup, one brown-black and one white
steps.cameraCheck: The cup with the coffee and sugar, next to the teaspoon
steps.videoShot: A level teaspoon of coffee being tipped into a cup.
steps.watchOut: Heaped spoons, which make the drink bitter or too sweet; level the spoons with a knife.

steps.title: Heat the water
steps.text: Warm 1 tbsp (15 ml) water until it is hot to the touch but not boiling.
steps.visualCue: Small bubbles start at the bottom and steam rises, but no rolling boil
steps.cameraCheck: The little pan or kettle with steam rising
steps.videoShot: Steam rising from a small pan of water.
steps.watchOut: Boiling water, which scorches instant coffee and gives a harsh, burnt taste; if it boils, let it cool for 30 seconds first.

steps.title: Dissolve the coffee
steps.text: Pour the warm water over the coffee and sugar and stir for about 30 seconds into a thick dark syrup.
steps.visualCue: No visible granules left; a glossy dark brown paste or syrup that smells strongly of coffee
steps.cameraCheck: The cup of smooth dark coffee syrup, with a spoon lifted out clean
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring until the coffee and sugar vanish into a dark syrup.
steps.watchOut: Undissolved granules and sugar crystals, which end up as a gritty layer at the bottom of the glass; keep stirring, and if lumps remain, add 1 tsp more warm water.

steps.title: Add the syrup and milk to the blender
steps.text: Pour the coffee syrup into the blender jar, then add the 200 ml cold milk.
steps.visualCue: The milk turns from white to a light brown swirl as it meets the syrup
steps.cameraCheck: The blender jar with the milk and coffee syrup in it
steps.videoShot: Dark coffee syrup swirling into white milk in the jar.
steps.watchOut: Filling the jar more than two-thirds full, so it leaks or spills when blending; one serving fits easily in a standard jar.

steps.title: Add the ice
steps.visualCue: The cubes float on top of the milk in the jar
steps.cameraCheck: The jar with 4 ice cubes visible
steps.videoShot: Ice cubes dropping into the jar.
steps.watchOut: Too many cubes, which water the drink down and give a thin taste; stay at 4 cubes, and if it is still thin, add a little more coffee and sugar.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Close the lid and blend for 20-30 seconds on high.
steps.tip: Hold the lid down firmly with a hand towel; the cold liquid and ice can pop the lid.
steps.visualCue: The drink turns an even light-coffee colour with a thick froth on top, and the ice is gone or only small bits are left
steps.cameraCheck: The blended drink in the jar showing froth on top
steps.videoShot: The jar blending, with froth rising at the top.
steps.watchOut: Blending too long, which melts the ice and flattens the froth (one source warns that blending too long or at very high speed works against a foamy drink); stop when there are no large ice pieces. If the froth is weak, the milk was not cold enough.

steps.title: Pour into the glass
steps.text: If you like, drizzle 1 tsp chocolate syrup inside the empty glass first, then pour the cold coffee in.
steps.visualCue: A tall glass filled to about 2 cm below the rim with a layer of froth on top, and (if used) dark streaks on the glass wall
steps.cameraCheck: The filled glass held in front of the camera
steps.videoShot: Cold coffee being poured down the side of a tall glass.
steps.watchOut: Pouring in a hurry so the froth overflows; tilt the glass a little and pour down the side.

steps.title: Serve at once
steps.text: Add a straw and drink straight away.
steps.visualCue: A light-brown frothy drink with condensation on the glass
steps.cameraCheck: The finished glass with froth on top
steps.videoShot: A straw going into the finished glass.
steps.watchOut: Letting it stand for more than 10-15 minutes, when the froth collapses and the ice melts into the milk; if it has stood, give it a quick stir or shake.

reasons: no oil or frying, no salt, and milk gives useful calcium (about 24% of the day), riboflavin and B12 with only about 185 kcal. Points off for about 15 g of added sugar (60% of the 25 g limit), no fibre, and about 90 mg of caffeine (est.). Restaurant glasses are bigger (350-400 ml), are often made with ice cream, chocolate syrup or whipped cream, and use more sugar, so about 300-400 kcal and 25-40 g sugar is likely (est.; a published café-style recipe shows 202 kcal and 24 g sugar, and ice-cream versions about 390 kcal).

researchRating.basis: a much-loved, very widely made café and home drink, with many Indian recipe sites and blogs publishing near-identical quick versions and a lot of positive comments about the froth and the five-minute method. Points off because results depend on instant-coffee brand and milk temperature, and because café versions are often very sweet. Recipe-site star counts were not checked this run. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Best fresh. If you must keep it, pour into a closed bottle and keep in the fridge for up to about 1 day (milk drink, keep it cold; not source-checked); shake before drinking because it separates and loses its froth. Not recommended for the freezer as a drink. Do not reheat.
leftoverRemix: Coffee ice cubes. Pour leftover cold coffee into an ice-cube tray and freeze for at least 4 hours; next time use these cubes in place of plain ice so the drink does not get watered down.
burnOff: about 2.6 km of running (185 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 3.7 km of brisk walking (about 45 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: Not found — no source seen on whether coffee is accepted in vrat; the other ingredients (milk, sugar) are normally allowed, but caffeine and instant coffee powder are treated differently by different families

ekadashi.reason: Not found — no source seen on coffee on Ekadashi; milk and sugar are not grains, but rules on caffeine differ by family

jain.reason: no roots, onion, garlic, meat, fish, egg or honey in the recipe

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; it contains about 90 mg caffeine (est.) and 15 g added sugar, and many people find caffeine makes them thirstier later in the day, so it is easier at iftar than at sehri (not source-checked)

jain.reason: milk, sugar, instant coffee and ice only; no onion, garlic, potato or other root vegetable, no egg, no honey

vegan.reason: the main recipe uses cow milk (200 ml); use oat, soy or almond milk (see Vegan variant)

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian recipe with no meat or egg

sattvik.reason: the recipe has no onion or garlic (note: coffee is a stimulant and some sattvik traditions avoid caffeine; that is a separate rule that was not source-checked)

glutenFree.reason: milk, coffee, sugar and ice; no wheat, rava, maida or hing (check the label if you add chocolate syrup or a flavoured coffee mix)

dairyFree.reason: milk; use the plant-milk version (see Dairy-free variant)

variants.reason: Main recipe already Jain (no onion, garlic, roots, egg or honey).
Main recipe already gluten-free (no wheat, rava, maida or hing; check labels on chocolate syrup).
